jordan: Quick question — if we need to emergency-disable the prod inference feature-flag (prod-llm), who is allowed to flip it and what breadcrumb/audit do we need to leave?
maya: TL;DR: SRE oncall + Eng leads + Security leads can flip. must open an incident and add a reason.
samir: +1. Oncall can flip for immediate mitigation. We expect a follow-up runbook entry in the INC ticket within 30m.
alex: Security policy: only people in the 'kill-switch' group or org admins. Also we require an explicit audit_reason and ticket id.
jordan: What about scope — can we do a partial canary disable (region or customer tier) or is it all-or-nothing?
maya: We have flag-scopes: region, customer_tier, and rollout_percent. Prefer partial when possible. Full off only for safety-critical outages.
samir: Example command we use in runbook:
```
# disable fully for 1h with audit note
redwoodctl feature toggle set prod-llm --state off --ttl 1h --audit "INC-9876 - latency spike"
```
jordan: Nice. Does that write to a centralized audit log automatically?
ops-bot: audit:feature_toggle: prod-llm toggled by samir at 2024-12-18T14:05:23Z reason="INC-9876 - latency spike" duration=3600s
alex: ops-bot confirms. All toggles are logged in Console -> Security -> Feature Flag Audit + forwarded to SSO audit pipeline. The audit record must include user, time, reason, and original incident link.
maya: Guardrails:
- toggles by oncall should be temporary (TTL <= 2h)
- must create follow-up task for root cause + permanent fix
- if toggle is global, notify product + trust teams within 15m

jordan: Escalation chain? If oncall flips but the outage persists or toggle has no effect?
samir: Escalate to SRE lead -> Eng platform lead -> CTO if still bad after 30m. Create a concurrent P0 and keep #incidents updated.
jordan: Who audits who flipped? E.g., if someone flips in panic, how do we trace?
alex: We correlate feature audit logs with the incident timeline and with git logs for any recent rollout. We also have automated alerts that DM the oncall manager when a global toggle occurs.
maya: Small operational note: don't use the old ad-hoc 'flip' endpoint (deprecated). Use redwoodctl or Console toggle UI so audit metadata is captured.
jordan: Any required labels in the incident ticket?
samir: Yep: severity, impacted_services (e.g., inference-api), approx_impact_percent, toggle_state_before, toggle_state_after, rollback_plan.
jordan: I'll update the runbook with the exact command and add the TTL guard. tagging @samir @alex for review.
maya: Thanks — small test suggestion: practice this during game-day next month (canary disable exercise). :thumbsup:
ops-bot: reminder: scheduled game-day: 2025-01-10 10:00 UTC — topic: feature-flag emergency drills :rotating_light:
alex: One last point: permission changes take ~5m to propagate. If you're trying to flip and get 403, ping SRE channel and escalate accordingly.
jordan: got it, thanks everyone. I'll post the updated runbook link in this thread when done.
